questions.title: What standard of review does the Federal Circuit apply to TTAB factual findings versus legal conclusions on appeal?
questions.question_body: I'm confused by the opinion’s statement that "We review the Board’s legal conclusions de novo, and its findings of fact for substantial evidence." How does this dual standard work in practice? Which elements of a likelihood‑of‑confusion analysis are considered "legal conclusions" and which are "findings of fact"? And how does "substantial evidence" differ from a "de novo" review when assessing the Board’s decision?

questions.title: Does the second DuPont factor require identical goods/services, or merely related ones? How does CC Serve’s partnership with banks affect this analysis?
questions.question_body: The court affirmed the Board’s finding that credit‑card services and banking/financing services are "highly similar" under the second DuPont factor, citing dictionary definitions. However, Apex argues that CC Serve only partners with banks and does not provide banking itself. In trademark law, how closely must the goods or services be related for this factor? Do partnerships or joint‑venture arrangements change the analysis of similarity?

questions.title: When applying the sixth DuPont factor, what scope of "similar marks" should be considered – only those used on identical goods, or also those used on related financial services?
questions.question_body: The opinion says the Board improperly limited consideration to nine Aspire‑formative marks used on credit‑card services and ignored 42 other marks used on broader banking/finance services. Under precedent, must the sixth factor consider all marks used on "similar" goods/services? How do courts define "similar" in this context, especially in a crowded financial‑services market?

questions.title: How does a trademark’s commercial strength or weakness influence its scope of protection under the first DuPont factor?
questions.question_body: The court vacated the Board’s first‑factor analysis because reconsideration of the sixth factor could affect the mark’s commercial impression. What role does commercial strength play in assessing similarity of appearance, sound, connotation, and overall impression? Why might an inherently distinctive mark still receive only a narrow scope if deemed weak?

questions.title: "Vacate in part, remand" – what exactly must the TTAB do on remand after such an order?
questions.question_body: The Federal Circuit vacated only its findings on factors six and one and remanded for reconsideration. Does this mean the Board must re‑evaluate those two factors only while leaving its other findings intact? Can it still reach a different overall likelihood‑of‑confusion conclusion after reweighing just those factors?

questions.title: Is it permissible for the TTAB to define "credit card services" after its removal from the USPTO ID Manual, and how is such a definition reviewed on appeal?
questions.question_body: The Board created its own definition of credit‑card services because that entry was deleted from the ID Manual. Is it within TTAB authority to craft such definitions ex nihilo? On appeal, what standard do courts apply when evaluating whether those definitions are valid or supported by substantial evidence?
